critical_code_review_comments: Solid design: single shared 60s scheduler loop, atomic Mongo compare-and-set on both `status` filter and `_autoNoShowApplied/_autoDeclineApplied` guard flags — losing-race writes are no-ops (verified via idempotency test).

audit.log_edge_case_action uses find_one + insert (not a true upsert with unique index enforcement); the unique-sparse index on idempotencyKey is the actual safety net. This double-check works because concurrent inserts on the same idempotency_key would fail the unique index — but the code currently does not catch DuplicateKeyError, so a rare race between the find_one and insert_one could raise. Low-risk but worth wrapping in try/except pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError → return False.

edge_case_scheduler.py lines 133-141 (auto no-show) and 264-272 (auto-decline) issue a second users.find_one immediately after the $inc update just to check whether performanceStrikes crossed 3. Could be collapsed into a single find_one_and_update returning the new doc — minor.

stripe.error module import path changed in newer stripe SDKs (>=7.x it's stripe.StripeError, not stripe.error.StripeError). Current code uses stripe.error.StripeError which still works via the legacy shim, but pin the version or migrate to the new path to avoid a surprise break.

config/edge_cases.py module-level constants are captured at import time; monkeypatching cfg.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in a test only affects the test-process copy, not the running server (test_webhook_bad_signature_rejected correctly documents this). Consider a lazy getter (e.g., def stripe_webhook_secret() -> str | None) for ops hot-reload if that's ever needed.
No unit test explicitly covers the sessionType=='virtual' skip branch of _job_auto_no_show_trainer (only en_route skip is tested). Coverage gap, non-blocking.
